questions.question: Which specific schedules under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 must a commercial bank take into account to fulfill obligations under government orders for Section 51A of UAPA and Section 12A of the WMD Act?
questions.answer: A commercial bank must take into account the lists in the First Schedule and the Fourth Schedule of the UAPA, 1967, including any amendments made to them.
questions.evidence: lists in the first schedule and the fourth schedule of UAPA, 1967 and any amendments to the same for compliance with the Government orders on implementation of section 51A of the UAPA and section 12A of the WMD Act.

unanswerable.question: What is the mandatory timeframe within which a commercial bank must update its internal customer screening database after an amendment is published to the Fourth Schedule of the UAPA, 1967?
unanswerable.why: Paragraph 59 mandates that commercial banks take into account the fourth schedule of UAPA and its amendments, but it does not specify any operational deadline or timeframe for updating internal screening systems.

questions.question: What foreign contribution statutory framework and regulatory directives are commercial banks required to adhere to?
questions.answer: Commercial banks must comply with the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010, and the rules framed under it. Additionally, banks are obligated to follow all communications and instructions issued by the RBI based on inputs from the Ministry of Home Affairs.
questions.evidence: The bank shall ensure adherence to the provisions of Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010, and Rules made thereunder. Further, the bank shall also ensure meticulous compliance with any instructions / communications on the matter issued from time to time by the RBI based on advice received from the Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India.

questions.question: Which Ministry's advice forms the basis for RBI directions issued to commercial banks regarding foreign contribution compliance?
questions.answer: RBI issues communications and instructions to commercial banks regarding foreign contribution compliance based on advice received from the Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India.
questions.evidence: Further, the bank shall also ensure meticulous compliance with any instructions / communications on the matter issued from time to time by the RBI based on advice received from the Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India.

unanswerable.question: What specific documents must a commercial bank collect from an NGO to verify its registration status under the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010?
unanswerable.why: Paragraph 64 mandates general adherence to the FCRA, 2010, and related RBI communications, but does not list any specific documentation or verification steps required for FCRA accounts.

questions.question: How frequently is a commercial bank required to review its internal Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing risk assessment?
questions.answer: A commercial bank must review its ML/TF risk assessment at least annually, with the exact periodicity decided by its Board or delegated committee in line with the assessment outcomes.
questions.evidence: Further, the Board or a committee of the Board to which it has delegated power shall determine the periodicity of the risk assessment exercise, in alignment with the outcome of the risk assessment exercise. However, the bank shall review it at least annually.

questions.question: Besides internal Board governance, which external entities must a commercial bank share its ML/TF risk assessment outcomes with?
questions.answer: A commercial bank is required to make the outcomes of its ML/TF risk assessment exercise available to self-regulating bodies as well as competent authorities.
questions.evidence: The bank shall present the outcome of the exercise to the Board or any committee of the Board to which power has been delegated in this regard. The outcome shall also be made available to competent authorities and self-regulating bodies.

unanswerable.question: Within how many business days following the close of the financial year must a commercial bank submit its documented ML/TF risk assessment report to the Reserve Bank of India?
unanswerable.why: Paragraph 10 mandates that the assessment be reviewed at least annually and made available to competent authorities, but it does not prescribe a specific deadline or window of business days for submitting the report.

questions.question: What procedure must a commercial bank follow if an existing customer explicitly submits a written refusal to provide their PAN, equivalent e-document, or Form No. 60?
questions.answer: The bank is required to close the customer's account and settle all related obligations after establishing their identity using applicable identification documents.
questions.evidence: if a customer having an existing account-based relationship with a bank gives in writing to the bank that they do not want to submit their PAN or equivalent e-document thereof or Form No. 60, the bank shall close the account and all obligations due in relation to the account shall be appropriately settled

questions.question: How are operations restricted in a loan account when a commercial bank temporarily ceases operations due to the customer's failure to submit a PAN or Form No. 60?
questions.answer: When operations are temporarily stopped on asset accounts like loan accounts, the commercial bank must permit only credit transactions.
questions.evidence: In case of asset accounts such as loan accounts, for the purpose of ceasing the operation in the account, only credits shall be allowed.

unanswerable.question: What is the exact cut-off date mandated by the Central Government for existing commercial bank account holders to submit their PAN or Form No. 60 before their accounts are restricted?
unanswerable.why: Paragraph 43 states that the submission must be done 'by such date which the Central Government may notify', but it does not specify the actual cut-off date or deadline.

questions.question: When a commercial bank provides an 'at par' cheque facility to co-operative banks, what ongoing monitoring and risk management duties must it perform?
questions.answer: The commercial bank must continuously monitor the facility and review the arrangements to evaluate potential exposure, specifically focusing on credit risk and reputational risk.
questions.evidence: The ‘at par’ cheque facility offered by the bank to co-operative banks shall be monitored and such arrangements be reviewed to assess the risks including credit risk and reputational risk arising therefrom.

questions.question: Does a commercial bank providing an at-par cheque facility have the authority to inspect the KYC and AML records of the client co-operative bank?
questions.answer: Yes, commercial banks extending at-par cheque facilities must retain the right to verify the client co-operative bank's or society's records for compliance with KYC and AML rules.
questions.evidence: The right to verify the records maintained by the customer cooperative banks / societies for compliance with the extant instructions on KYC and AML under such arrangements shall be retained by bank.

unanswerable.question: How frequently is a commercial bank required to review its at-par cheque facility arrangements with co-operative banks?
unanswerable.why: Paragraph 78 mandates that commercial banks review at-par cheque arrangements to assess credit and reputational risk, but it does not specify a time frame or frequency (such as annual or quarterly) for these reviews.

questions.question: If a customer requests a fund transfer of ₹50,000 via NEFT or IMPS at a commercial bank, can the branch accept cash for this transaction?
questions.answer: No, commercial banks cannot accept cash payments for fund remittances or travellers' cheques valued at ₹50,000 and above. Such transfers must be completed by debiting the customer's account or against cheques.
questions.evidence: Any remittance of funds by way of demand draft, mail / telegraphic transfer / NEFT / IMPS or any other mode and issue of travellers’ cheques for value of ₹50,000 and above shall be effected by debit to the customer’s account or against cheques and not against cash payment.

questions.question: Is a commercial bank obligated to print the buyer's name on instruments like demand drafts or banker's cheques?
questions.answer: Yes, commercial banks are required to include the purchaser's name on the front of demand drafts, pay orders, banker's cheques, and similar instruments.
questions.evidence: Further, the bank shall incorporate the name of the purchaser on the face of the demand draft, pay order, banker’s cheque, etc., by the issuing bank.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum limit on cash remittances allowed per day for transactions below ₹50,000 at a commercial bank?
unanswerable.why: Paragraph 75 prohibits cash payments for remittances of ₹50,000 and above, but it does not specify any daily cap or conditions for cash remittances under ₹50,000.

questions.question: If a jurisdiction is listed in an FATF statement, is a commercial bank completely prohibited from engaging in any trade or business transactions with entities from that region?
questions.answer: No, commercial banks are permitted to continue legitimate business and trade transactions with entities from jurisdictions listed in FATF statements, provided appropriate due diligence is followed.
questions.evidence: The processes referred to in (1) and (2) above do not preclude the bank from having legitimate trade and business transactions with the countries and jurisdictions mentioned in the FATF statement.

questions.question: What documentation and audit trail requirements apply to a commercial bank when dealing with transactions involving entities from non-compliant FATF jurisdictions?
questions.answer: A commercial bank must analyze the background and intent of such transactions, preserve written findings along with all relevant documents, and present them to the RBI or other regulators upon request.
questions.evidence: The bank shall examine the background and purpose of transactions with persons (including legal persons and other financial institutions) from jurisdictions included in FATF Statements and countries that do not or insufficiently apply the FATF Recommendations, retain written findings together with all documents, and make them available to the RBI / other relevant authorities, on request.

unanswerable.question: For how many years must a commercial bank retain the written findings and supporting documentation for transactions conducted with parties in FATF-listed countries?
unanswerable.why: Paragraph 61 states that banks must retain written findings and documents and make them available on request, but it does not specify a concrete retention period or number of years.

questions.question: Can a commercial bank clear an account payee cheque for a party other than the specified payee?
questions.answer: Commercial banks are prohibited from collecting account payee cheques for anyone other than the payee constituent, except for certain cheques not exceeding ₹50,000 collected for co-operative credit societies.
questions.evidence: The bank shall not collect account payee cheques for any person other than the payee constituent.

questions.question: What is the monetary limit up to which a commercial bank may collect account payee cheques for a co-operative credit society whose constituents are the payees?
questions.answer: A commercial bank may optionally collect account payee cheques up to a limit not exceeding ₹50,000 for its co-operative credit society customers, provided the payees belong to those societies.
questions.evidence: The bank shall, at its option, collect account payee cheques drawn for an amount not exceeding ₹50,000 to the account of its customers who are co-operative credit societies, provided the payees of such cheques are the constituents of such co-operative credit societies.

unanswerable.question: What specific penalty or monetary fine does a commercial bank face if it collects an account payee cheque exceeding ₹50,000 for a co-operative credit society?
unanswerable.why: Paragraph 69 specifies the prohibition and the ₹50,000 ceiling for co-operative credit societies, but it does not detail any specific fines, penalties, or disciplinary actions for violating this limit.

questions.question: When is a commercial bank obligated to implement countermeasures based on directives from international or intergovernmental bodies?
questions.answer: A commercial bank must undertake countermeasures when requested by an international or intergovernmental organization of which India is a member, provided the Central Government has accepted that organization.
questions.evidence: The bank shall undertake countermeasures when called upon so to do by any international or intergovernmental organisation of which India is a member and which is accepted by the Central Government.

unanswerable.question: Within how many days of receiving a notice from an approved intergovernmental organization must a commercial bank implement the mandated countermeasures?
unanswerable.why: Paragraph 60 specifies the obligation to undertake countermeasures when called upon by an accepted organization of which India is a member, but it does not specify any time limit or deadline for implementation.

questions.question: Does compliance with the RBI KYC Directions override or replace other existing laws and regulatory frameworks applicable to a commercial bank?
questions.answer: No, the RBI KYC Directions operate alongside other existing legal requirements. They are meant to supplement, rather than repeal or diminish, any other laws, rules, or directions currently in force for commercial banks.
questions.evidence: The provisions of these Directions shall be in addition to, and not in derogation of the provisions of any other laws, rules, regulations, or directions, for the time being in force.

unanswerable.question: If an explicit conflict arises between the RBI KYC Directions and another prevailing statute applicable to a commercial bank, which specific law takes precedence?
unanswerable.why: The text states that the Directions are in addition to and not in derogation of other laws, but it does not specify a conflict-resolution rule or state which law overrides the other in the event of a direct contradiction.

questions.question: For which customer types is a commercial bank permitted to use the Video-based Customer Identification Process (V-CIP) during new account onboarding?
questions.answer: Commercial banks can use V-CIP to carry out customer due diligence for onboarding individual customers, proprietors of proprietorship firms, and authorised signatories and beneficial owners of legal entity customers.
questions.evidence:
The bank may undertake V-CIP to carry out:
(1) CDD in case of new customer onboarding for individual customers, proprietor in case of proprietorship firm, authorised signatories and Beneficial Owners (BOs) in case of Legal Entity (LE) customers.

questions.question: When a commercial bank conducts customer due diligence for a proprietorship firm via V-CIP, what additional document must it collect alongside the proprietor's verification?
questions.answer: Besides verifying the proprietor, the commercial bank must collect equivalent e-documents supporting the business activity proofs of the proprietorship firm.
questions.evidence: Provided that in case of CDD of a proprietorship firm, the bank shall also obtain the equivalent e-document of the activity proofs with respect to the proprietorship firm, as mentioned in paragraph 31 and paragraph 32, apart from undertaking CDD of the proprietor.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum permissible time duration for a commercial bank to complete a V-CIP session with a customer?
unanswerable.why: Paragraph 26 lists the permitted purposes for conducting V-CIP (such as new customer onboarding, account conversion, and periodic KYC updates), but does not state any timeframe, duration limit, or technical deadline for completing a V-CIP session.

questions.question: What objective must a commercial bank fulfill when conducting ongoing due diligence on its account holders?
questions.answer: A commercial bank must perform ongoing due diligence to ensure that customer transactions remain aligned with the bank's knowledge regarding the customer, their business, risk profile, and source of funds or wealth.
questions.evidence: The bank shall undertake ongoing due diligence of customers to ensure that their transactions are consistent with their knowledge about the customers, customers’ business and risk profile, the source of funds / wealth.

questions.question: Which customer parameters must a commercial bank compare transactions against during ongoing monitoring?
questions.answer: When monitoring transactions, a commercial bank must compare them against its existing knowledge of the customer, the customer's business activities, their risk profile, and their source of funds or wealth.
questions.evidence: ensure that their transactions are consistent with their knowledge about the customers, customers’ business and risk profile, the source of funds / wealth.

unanswerable.question: At what specific time intervals or periodic frequencies must a commercial bank update ongoing due diligence records for high-risk customers?
unanswerable.why: Paragraph 39 mandates ongoing due diligence to ensure transactions match customer risk profiles and sources of funds, but it does not state any fixed timeframes or periodic schedules for updating these records.

questions.question: How many documents confirming business activity must a commercial bank collect when verifying a sole proprietary firm?
questions.answer: A commercial bank is required to collect any two of the prescribed documents (or equivalent e-documents) as proof of business or activity registered in the name of the proprietary firm.
questions.evidence: In addition to the above, the bank shall also obtain any two of the following documents or the equivalent e-documents thereof as proof of business / activity in the name of the proprietary firm:

questions.question: If a sole proprietor provides an Income Tax Return to a commercial bank as proof of business, will an ITR acknowledgement receipt alone fulfill the requirement?
questions.answer: No, an acknowledgement alone is not sufficient; the bank must receive the complete Income Tax Return reflecting the firm's income, authenticated or acknowledged by the Income Tax authorities.
questions.evidence: Complete Income Tax Return (not just the acknowledgement) in the name of the sole proprietor where the firm's income is reflected, duly authenticated / acknowledged by the Income Tax authorities

unanswerable.question: Can a commercial bank open an account for a newly incorporated sole proprietary firm using only one proof of business document if the firm has been in operation for under six months?
unanswerable.why: Paragraph 31 strictly mandates obtaining any two of the listed documents as proof of business/activity, without stating any exemptions, relaxations, or alternative conditions for newly formed or young proprietary firms.
